minutes.headline: Capital committee reviewed the interim manager's revised FY26 capital plan; split over Town Hall HVAC/windows and the school generator; no vote.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the interim Town Manager's revised funding sources and recommended warrant list, and debated where it departs from the committee's rankings: Town Hall HVAC and windows, the primary school generator and the catch basin truck. It also discussed a possible track and field engineering article, future meeting topics and a report in the warrant book. The only vote was adjournment; the December 16th minutes were tabled.

public_comment.topic: Public comment opened; thanks to the committee and the interim manager for the session.
Warned that several possible borrowings cannot all hit the budget at once without breaching borrowing policy limits, and urged keeping Town Hall envelope repairs in the plan.

votes.motion: Approval of December 16th minutes: tabled, no vote taken

votes.outcome: passed; roll call heard as Mr Alonzo, Bowen, Mr Brer, and the chair, all in favor

budget_items.what_was_said: Interim manager had hoped for about this much for capital after reserve contributions, snow and ice and a grant deficit; later pushed lower.

budget_items.topic: Debt service and returned demolition money
budget_items.what_was_said: Debt is going down slightly; budgeted money for demolishing the old primary school is returned because state grants cover it.
Interim manager's practice is to roll over a portion of the Omnibus budget as working capital; a remainder of free cash stays unallocated.
Recommended list differs from CPC numbers, partly because of the primary school generator revision; total near the revised figure.
Crack sealing now and resurfacing in a couple of years instead of full paving.
Five-year lease could shift to a possible stormwater district; interest cost described as nominal.
Estimate rose from under one figure to over another; members said ranking might have dropped.
Estimated cost to decommission the central and north wings is paid from free cash, reducing capital.
Interim manager added a contingency to the specific items.
School five-year plan carried a two-year project; proposal is to fund engineering to be bid ready, with borrowing at fall town meeting.
Resident cited non-exempt borrowing policy limit and said current debt is low.

decisions.decision: Chair will schedule a meeting on standardizing request forms and contact the new town manager about five-year plan and policy timing.
Committee to include a report in the warrant book (deadline mentioned as March 20); no warrant article required.
Interim manager will revisit the capital plan, including the generator and Town Hall items, the next day.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee took no votes on the revised FY26 capital plan; its only vote was to adjourn, and the December 16th minutes were tabled.
The interim Town Manager's recommended warrant list departs from the committee's own rankings on Town Hall HVAC and windows, the primary school generator and the catch basin truck.
The primary school generator estimate rose, and members said its ranking might have dropped; the interim manager will revisit the plan, including the generator and Town Hall items, the next day.
Decommissioning the central and north wings of TC Passos is estimated to be paid from free cash, which reduces the amount available for capital.
The committee will put a report in the warrant book with no article required, and the chair will schedule a meeting on standardizing request forms.

why_it_matters: The warrant list that goes to Town Meeting may not match the committee's own ranking, so the Town Hall envelope repairs and the school generator are still undecided items that residents could be asked to fund.

Free cash used for the TC Passos decommissioning is not available for capital projects, and a resident warned at public comment that several possible borrowings together could breach the town's borrowing policy limits.
